items.title: A client with suspected DVT should not have the affected leg ___. The nurse should assess for pulmonary embolism symptoms such as sudden ___ and chest pain.
items.rationale: Massage is avoided because of embolization concern. Sudden dyspnea and chest pain may indicate PE and require emergency evaluation.

items.title: A client is found unresponsive with RR 5/min, pinpoint pupils, and suspected opioid exposure. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:opioid overdose with respiratory depression|actions:provide airway and ventilatory support;administer naloxone and repeat per protocol if needed|monitor:respiratory rate and oxygenation;level of consciousness and recurrent sedation
items.rationale: Ventilation is the immediate priority. Naloxone reverses opioid effects but may wear off before the opioid, so monitor for recurrence.

items.title: Highlight findings suggesting acute kidney injury: rising creatinine;reduced urine output;new hyperkalemia;stable baseline creatinine;new fluid overload.
items.content: segments:rising creatinine|reduced urine output|new hyperkalemia|stable baseline creatinine|new fluid overload|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Rising creatinine, oliguria, hyperkalemia, and fluid overload are complications or indicators of acute kidney injury.

items.title: A client is prescribed 1.2 g of an antibiotic. The vial concentration after reconstitution is 400 mg/mL. How many mL are needed?
A client's lactate decreases from 5.2 to 4.7 to 4.5 mmol/L after initial treatment but remains elevated. What is the best interpretation?
items.content: Perfusion may be improving slowly but remains abnormal; continue reassessment and prescribed sepsis management.
items.rationale: A downward trend is encouraging, but persistent elevation may indicate ongoing hypoperfusion or other causes and needs continued evaluation.

items.title: A client with a tibial fracture in a cast reports escalating pain despite medication. The calf is tense, pain increases with passive stretch, and sensation is tingling. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Notify the orthopedic surgeon immediately, perform and document neurovascular checks, keep the limb at heart level, and prepare for urgent cast release or fasciotomy as directed.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion, passive-stretch pain, tense swelling, and paresthesia suggest compartment syndrome. Delay can cause irreversible muscle and nerve injury.
